ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Cylindrical concrete pipes of the same specifications are transported by large trucks. The truck can load two layers of pipes. The bottom layer of pipes is fixed in the truck bed, and the top layer of pipes is stacked on the bottom layer. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the concrete pipes is given as $\mu=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$. The magnitude of the truck's acceleration during emergency braking is $8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. The mass of each concrete pipe is $m=1500\mathrm{kg}$, and the acceleration due to gravity is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. When the truck is traveling at a uniform velocity on a straight, horizontal road, determine the magnitude of the elastic force between pipes A and B in Figure 2.
2. If the truck is traveling at a uniform velocity of $43.2\mathrm{km/h}$ on a horizontal road, calculate the minimum initial distance between the front of the top layer of pipes and the cab, such that the top layer of pipes does not collide with the cab during emergency braking.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cylindrical concrete pipes of the same specifications are transported by large trucks. The truck can load two layers of pipes. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 in the figure is a side view of a truck, and the carriage is loaded with long cylindrical pipes placed along the direction of the vehicle body; Figure 2 is a cross-sectional view of a pipe end face, with equal-radius circular pipes closely stacked in two layers, the lower layer at the bottom of the carriage, the upper-left pipe labeled A, and the lower-left pipe labeled B. A is located between two lower-layer pipes and is in contact with them, so the contact normals from the two lower-layer pipes pointing toward A are symmetric about the vertical direction, and each makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal direction. Then reason: When traveling uniformly in a straight line, A is subject to gravity mg and the supporting forces N given to it by the two lower-layer pipes. The horizontal components cancel each other, and vertical equilibrium gives: 2N sin60° = mg, so N = mg/(2 sin60°) = mg/√3. Substituting m=1500 kg, g=10 m/s² gives N=15000/√3=5000√3 N, so the elastic force between A and B is 5000√3 N. During emergency braking, from Figure 1 it can be known that the pipe axis is along the direction of the vehicle body, and the top-layer pipe slides axially relative to the lower-layer pipes. Each upper-layer pipe contacts two lower-layer pipes, and the kinetic friction force at each contact is μN, so the total braking friction force on the top-layer pipe is 2μN. Its deceleration a_p = 2μN/m = 2(√3/3)(mg/√3)/m = 2g/3 = 20/3 m/s². The initial speed 43.2 km/h = 12 m/s. The truck braking distance s_t = v²/(2×8)=144/16=9.0 m; the top-layer pipe braking distance s_p = v²/[2×(20/3)] = 144/(40/3)=10.8 m. The top-layer pipe travels 10.8-9.0=1.8 m more than the truck, so the minimum initial distance is 1.8 m.
